pretax.text: We reported $18 million of income before income tax under GAAP for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $111 million for the third quarter of 2025. Refer below for a more detailed discussion of the items impacting these results.

net.text: • Pretax income (loss), net income (loss), and earnings (loss) per share are presented on an adjusted basis. Adjustments are made for special charges that are unusual or nonrecurring in nature, as well as for gains and losses on foreign debt, as these adjustments enhance comparability of our core operations to prior periods and to the rest of the airline industry.

ocf.text: Cash provided by operating activities was $755 million during the first nine months of 2026, compared to $1.1 billion during the first nine months of 2025. The $309 million decrease was primarily driven by higher fuel prices throughout the year, partially offset by increased cash collected from advance ticket sales and other favorable working capital changes.

capex.text: Capital expenditures to acquire aircraft, flight equipment, and other property and equipment are the primary use of our investing cash flow. In 2026, we plan to incur approximately $1.6 billion in capital expenditures. We discuss our aircraft-related commitments in more detail below.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Loyalty program revenue, including that in the Passenger revenue line item in the consolidated statements of operations, represented approximately 16% of Air Group's total revenue in 2025.
Our codeshare and interline agreements generated approximately 5% of our total operating revenue for each of the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023.
In 2025, 74% of our total sales were conducted direct to customer with the remaining 26% through traditional and online travel agencies.
We rely on vendors and third parties for certain critical activities and sourcing, which could expose us to disruptions in our operation or unexpected cost increases.

We rely on vendors for a variety of services and functions critical to our business, including airframe and engine maintenance, regional flying, ground handling, fueling, computer reservation system hosting, telecommunication systems, information technology infrastructure and services, and deicing, among others.
We rely on partner airlines for codeshare and loyalty program marketing arrangements.
Additionally, we rely on partners to provide available space for credit redemption on their aircraft.
The Company’s ability to utilize these NOLs depends on generating sufficient taxable income in future periods.
We heavily depend on automated systems to operate our business.
Additionally, we rely on the FAA and its systems for critical aspects of flight operations.
Cash provided by ticket sales and from our co-branded credit card agreements are the primary sources of our operating cash flow.
Advance ticket sales and our co-branded credit card agreements are the primary sources of our operating cash flow.
Cash provided by new financing arrangements is the primary source of our financing cash flow.
Loyalty points are earned through travel, purchases using one of the Atmos Rewards or Hawaiian Airlines co-branded credit cards and purchases from other participating partners.
Ticket revenue is recorded as Passenger revenue, and represents the primary source of the Company's revenue.
